small_guidance:
- The GEMM uses `allow_tf32=False` which forces slower FP32 mma; switch to `allow_tf32=True` (inputs are fp32 random in [0,1), well within tf32 precision for this 5e-2 tolerance) — this alone should roughly halve the GEMM time on the 4090.
- Expand the autotune list with larger K tiles (BLOCK_K=128) and try `num_stages=4-5` with `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256` since K=8192 is large; also add a `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=128` config for better L2 reuse.
- In the group-norm kernel, CPG=512 → BLOCK=512; bump `num_warps=8` and consider `num_stages=2` and using `tl.sum` with the mask-then-zero trick already present; also fold the reduction by loading x once into registers and reusing (already done) — main win is ensuring the load is fully coalesced (it is, since rows are contiguous).
large_guidance:
- Use a split-K or persistent GEMM with tf32 (or even fp16 accumulate-to-fp32 cast on input) to dramatically cut the 1024×8192×8192 matmul cost, which dominates 4.65 ms; alternatively dispatch to cuBLAS via `torch.addmm` for the GEMM and only keep a custom fused GN+HardTanh kernel — cuBLAS tf32 on a 4090 will beat a hand-tuned Triton fp32 GEMM at this size.
- Fuse the bias add into the GroupNorm kernel instead of the GEMM epilogue: have the GEMM produce raw `x@W^T`, then in the GN kernel load `bias` once per group and add before computing mean/var — this removes one global write/read and lets the GEMM run as a pure cuBLAS call.
- Consider a two-stage GN kernel for CPG=512: stage-1 computes per-(sample,group) mean/rstd with one program per group using a wider BLOCK and warp-shuffle reduction; stage-2 (or same kernel persistent) applies affine+hardtanh. With only 16 groups × 1024 samples = 16384 programs, persistence is unnecessary, but increasing warps to 8 and using vectorized fp32x4 loads will saturate bandwidth.
